# Ancient Nerds

> An interactive 3D globe and open research platform for archaeology. 1.76 million
> site records aggregated from public datasets, of which about 4,900 are curated by
> hand across 91 countries, plus AI-written story summaries, weekly journals and
> open-access research papers.

Operated by Dominiak Consulting. Contact: contact@ancientnerds.com

## How to read this site

Most pages are server-rendered and readable without JavaScript. The interactive
globe at /globe.html is a WebGL application and has no text equivalent — the
country and site pages below carry the same records as prose.

## Provenance and reliability

- **Site records** (/sites/) are human-curated and reviewed. A description is
  either sentences selected from the site's English Wikipedia article (CC BY-SA,
  attributed on the page with the revision it comes from) or a text an AI system
  wrote from cited sources, marked as such. Each page names its source; pages with
  a Wikidata item link it in their structured data (sameAs).
- **Stories** (/news-archive/) are AI-written summaries of archaeology videos
  from third-party YouTube channels. They report what a video says, including
  claims archaeologists dispute; they are secondary sources about secondary
  sources: useful as pointers to the video, not as citations for its claims.
  Each carries a visible AI-generated notice and a machine-readable
  data-ai-generated="true" marker.
- **Research papers** (/research/) are produced by an AI pipeline with citation
  checking, published under CC BY 4.0. Most name the organisation as author, a
  few a person. Treat their reference lists as the citable part.
- **Journals** (/articles/) are AI-written weekly digests of the stories.
- Stories in the speculative category are labelled as such and kept out of
  search indexes (noindex) rather than removed.

If you cite this site, prefer the curated site pages and the reference lists of
the research papers over the AI-written narrative text.

## Main entry points

- [Sites by country](https://ancientnerds.com/sites/): about 4,900 curated sites, 91 countries
- [Story Archive](https://ancientnerds.com/news-archive/): over 2,200 archaeology stories
- [Research Library](https://ancientnerds.com/research/): open-access papers, CC BY 4.0
- [Weekly Journal](https://ancientnerds.com/articles/): weekly digests
- [Search](https://ancientnerds.com/search.html): full-text search across all records
- [3D Globe](https://ancientnerds.com/globe.html): the interactive map
- [Sitemap](https://ancientnerds.com/sitemap.xml): about 7,300 content URLs

## Machine-readable data

- Public API, for example https://ancientnerds.com/api/v1/sites/search,
  /api/v1/sites/{site_id}, /api/v1/sources and /api/v1/research
- OpenAPI description: https://ancientnerds.com/api/v1/openapi.json
- API documentation: https://ancientnerds.com/api.html

## Licensing

Site records and research papers: CC BY 4.0 — attribution to Ancient Nerds
(https://ancientnerds.com) required. A site description taken from Wikipedia
stays under CC BY-SA 4.0, as attributed on its page. Images come from Wikimedia Commons and
other original sources under their own licences, named on each page; they are
not covered by the CC BY 4.0 grant and are not AI-generated.
